name: The thirty-six principles (ṣaṭtriṃśat-tattva)

definitions.definition: Manifestation from Śiva to earth in thirty-six levels: five pure (Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, Śuddhavidyā), the impure boundary of Māyā with its five sheaths (kalā, vidyā, rāga, kāla, niyati), then the Sāṃkhya series from Puruṣa to earth. All shine in the supreme like images in a mirror (Paramārthasāra 11-13).

relations.note: tattvas 12-36 correspond to Sāṃkhya's twenty-five; the Śaivas add eleven above them

notes: The order of the kañcukas varies slightly between sources (e.g. kāla and niyati).

definitions.definition: Kalā, vidyā, rāga, kāla and niyati, which with māyā limit universal agency, knowledge, fullness, eternity and pervasion into the individual's 'only a little, only this, only now, only here' (Paramārthasāra 16-17).

The ultimate is light (prakāśa) whose very nature is reflexive awareness (vimarśa); without vimarśa light would be insentient like a crystal (ĪPK 1.5.11); vimarśa is supreme speech and freedom (1.5.13).

The ultimate as dynamic, pulsing awareness - opening and closing (unmeṣa-nimeṣa) - on which all particular movements rest, never lost in any state, and graspable in intense moments and in the gap between thoughts.
Everything is a manifestation (ābhāsa) of consciousness within itself, appearing as if external; the world is real as manifestation and unfolded on consciousness's own screen by its will.

relations.note: Advaita's apparent transformation; the Kashmir Śaivas hold manifestation to be real and free

definitions.definition: The absolute freedom of consciousness, its primary sovereignty, by which it manifests, conceals and reveals (ĪPK 1.5.13; PH 1).

name: The reflection doctrine (pratibimbavāda) of the Trika

definitions.definition: The universe appears in consciousness as a city in a mirror - undivided from the mirror yet appearing distinct - but, unlike a mirror, consciousness is itself the source of the image (TĀ 3; Paramārthasāra 12-13).

Emission, maintenance, withdrawal, concealment and grace; the bound individual performs them too - as manifesting, relishing, reflecting, planting the seed and dissolving (PH 10-11); bondage and liberation are Śiva's play (Paramārthasāra 33).
Āṇava: loss of freedom or awareness; māyīya: the appearance of separate knowables; kārma: agency in an unconscious agent; all through the power of māyā (ĪPK 3.2.4-5).
The root impurity is ignorance, not a substance; knowledge alone liberates (TĀ 1.22-26).

name: The four means (upāya)

definitions.definition: Anupāya (no means: realization by the teacher's word), śāmbhava (thought-free immersion), śākta (contemplation with the mind alone), āṇava (breath, seals, visualization, letters, places); graded by the intensity of grace; liberation is the same whatever the means (MVT 2.21-23; TĀ 1.165-170, chs. 2-5).

notes: The path map itself is pth:kashmir-four-upayas (owned by U51).

definitions.definition: For the most intensely graced, one hearing of the teacher's word reveals one's ever-present nature; nothing is to be done (TĀ 2; Śivadṛṣṭi 7.5-6; Anuttarāṣṭikā).

name: The three powers: will, knowledge, action

definitions.definition: Icchā, jñāna and kriyā, identified with the goddesses Parā, Parāparā and Aparā (TĀ 1.271-272); knowing and acting are the life of the living (ĪPK 1.1.4).

name: The five powers: consciousness, bliss, will, knowledge, action

definitions.definition: Cit, ānanda, icchā, jñāna, kriyā - the powers of Śiva that appear as the five pure tattvas (Paramārthasāra 14).

The goddesses Parā, Parāparā, Aparā (with Bhairava; Kālasaṅkarṣiṇī above them in Abhinavagupta's Trika); Śiva, Śakti and Nara; will, knowledge and action; non-difference, difference-in-non-difference, difference.

The fifty letters in natural order (mātṛkā, A to KṢA) as the emanation of the tattvas (Parātrīśikā 5-9), and in the scrambled order mālinī uniting vowels and consonants (Śiva and Śakti); the ground of limited knowledge when unrecognized (Śiva Sūtra 1.4) and of liberation when awakened by the teacher (2.7).

Parā (supreme speech = reflexive awareness itself, ĪPK 1.5.13), paśyantī, madhyamā and vaikharī; the Kashmir Śaivas add parā above the grammarians' three and deny that paśyantī is ultimate (Śivadṛṣṭi 2.1).
Liberation as recognition: the Lord is already one's self but unnoticed through delusion; revealing his powers brings recognition, as a woman recognizes the lover beside her (ĪPK 1.1.3, 4.17).
The Heart of Bhairava, seed of the universe (Parātrīśikā 24); the heart-space of meditation (VBT 49).
Consciousness as vibrancy is 'the Heart of the Supreme' (ĪPK 1.5.14).
The central consciousness whose unfolding gives the bliss of consciousness (PH 17-18).
The gap between breaths, cognitions, pleasure and pain, where reality shines (VBT 24-26, 61-62, 103, 126).
The unmeṣa between one thought and the next (SK 3.9).

name: The states: waking, dream, deep sleep, the fourth and beyond

definitions.definition: Waking is cognition, dream thought-construct, deep sleep non-discrimination (Śiva Sūtra 1.8-10); the fourth is enjoyed amid them and to be poured into them like oil (1.7, 3.20); spanda never departs in any state (SK 1.3).
Correlated with the breaths: prāṇa/apāna in waking and dream, samāna in sleep, udāna in the fourth, vyāna beyond (ĪPK 3.2.19-20).

relations.note: the Māṇḍūkya's scheme; the Śaivas add turyātīta

definitions.definition: Śiva, mantramaheśvara, mantreśvara, mantra, vijñānākala, pralayākala, sakala - graded by their impurities: the vijñānākala has only āṇava, the pralayākala āṇava and kārma, the sakala all three (ĪPK 3.2.6-10; TĀ 10).

name: The self as consciousness; the individual as contracted Śiva

definitions.definition: The self is consciousness (Śiva Sūtra 1.1); the individual is consciousness contracted, containing the universe in contracted form (PH 4), and the mind is consciousness descended (PH 5).

name: The three coverings of the self

definitions.definition: The subtle covering of impurity (mala), the gross covering of the kañcukas from māyā, and the outer body: the self wrapped in three sheaths (Paramārthasāra 24).

name: The five vital breaths in the Kashmirian scheme

definitions.definition: Prāṇa and apāna (waking and dream), samāna (deep sleep), udāna (the fourth, fiery, rising in the centre), vyāna (beyond, all-pervading) (ĪPK 3.2.19-20); in the āṇava practice they carry the seven blisses (TĀ 5.43-52).

name: The subtle body of the Netratantra

definitions.definition: Six wheels, sixteen supports, three targets and five voids (Netra 7.1), pierced in subtle meditation.

The paths of the denoting - letters, mantras, words - and of the denoted - kalās (nivṛtti, pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śānti, śāntyatītā), tattvas, worlds; purified in initiation and contemplated from gross to supreme (TĀ 6-12; VBT 56-57).

name: Cosmology: space, time and the worlds

definitions.definition: The path of space (deśādhvan): the worlds from Kālāgni to the highest, measured and ordered within the tattvas (TĀ 8); the path of time (kālādhvan): the cycles of time mirrored in the movement of the breath (TĀ 6); the world as the Lord's play and as phases of cognition.

name: The grades of the descent of power (śaktipāta)

definitions.definition: Grace depends on the Lord's freedom alone; intense, middling and mild, each in three degrees (nine grades); its signs are devotion to Rudra, mantra-success, control of beings, completion of undertakings and poetic power with sudden knowledge of scripture (MVT 2.14-16; TĀ 13); graded by scripture (TĀ 13.300-301).

notes: Nine-grade scheme recalled from TĀ 13 / Tantrasāra 11 (chapter level).

definitions.definition: The teacher is the means (Śiva Sūtra 2.6); the revelation of the Śiva Sūtra and its lineage (Kṣemarāja; Bhāskara, Vārttika 1.3-9).
Secrecy and qualification: the teaching is for those devoted to the teacher, heroic and thought-free (VBT 157-160); the lineage from Śrīkaṇṭha and Durvāsas (Śivadṛṣṭi 7.107-122).

name: Liberation while living (jīvanmukti) in Kashmir Śaivism

definitions.definition: Firm realization of oneness with consciousness while the body is experienced (PH 16); the liberated sees all as his own glory and regards the knowable as not different from himself (ĪPK 4.12-13).
The liberated acts without taint, his conduct free of rule, his worship inner (Paramārthasāra 61, 69-80).

relations.note: shared name; the Kashmir Śaivas add that the world is known as one's own real manifestation

name: Karma and rebirth in Kashmir Śaivism

definitions.definition: Karma bound by false knowledge perishes in the fire of knowledge like a roasted seed; the knower is untouched by merit and demerit; the one who dies midway on the path enjoys higher worlds and completes the path in another birth (Paramārthasāra 55-62, 96-102).

For the knower the place and manner of death do not matter - even without memory, in a holy place or an outcaste's house, he is liberated at the moment of knowledge (Paramārthasāra 83); the last moment only assists the deluded (90); funerary rites and a rite of immediate departure exist for initiates (TĀ 19, 24-25).

Rules and prohibitions are equal for the knower; purity as prescribed by the half-knowing is impurity in Śiva's view (VBT 123); rules based on difference are not direct means (TĀ 4); the Mata rejects the samaya rules (TĀ 4.262); equanimity toward friend and foe (VBT 125).

name: Powers and the warnings about them

definitions.definition: Powers arise from union with power and pure knowledge (Śiva Sūtra 1.19-21; SK 3.1-7), but powers under the veil of delusion are not liberation (Śiva Sūtra 3.6; 2.4; 3.23); light, sound, form and taste arising from the unmeṣa distract (SK 3.10).
The fruits listed for one established in a dhāraṇā (VBT 140-142).
Bliss, leaping up, trembling, sleep and whirling (MVT 11.35; TĀ 5.107).

name: The seven blisses of the breath

definitions.definition: Nijānanda, nirānanda, parānanda, brahmānanda, mahānanda, cidānanda, jagadānanda (TĀ 5.43-52).
The perfect 'I' whose essence is light and bliss, the potency of the great mantra (PH 20); the 'aham' spans the letters from A to HA (PTV).

name: Pure reasoning and the purification of thought

definitions.definition: In the śākta means thought is purified by pure reasoning, the teacher and scripture until the pure thought 'I am Śiva' becomes thought-free (TĀ 4).
The self is a dancer, the inner self the stage, the senses the spectators (Śiva Sūtra 3.9-11).

name: The hierarchy of revelations

definitions.definition: Veda < Śaiva (Siddhānta) < Vāma < Dakṣiṇa < Mata < Kula < Kaula < Trika (verse quoted by Jayaratha on TĀ 13.301; TĀ 13.300-301 grades grace in the same order); the Trika is the essence of all scripture (TĀ 1.18); all philosophies are stages of the one consciousness (PH 8).

notes: A variant quoted in the Parātrīśikāvivaraṇa places Kula before Mata.

definitions.definition: Kula is the totality of powers (Śakti), Akula Śiva beyond it; consciousness finally dissolves into the Akula abode (TĀ 4.170); the Kaula rule dwells in Bhairava's heart (Parātrīśikā 4).

name: The Kula ritual as interpreted by Abhinavagupta (summary)

definitions.definition: Tantrāloka 29 treats the secret Kula worship with a consort and Kaula substances as the outward form of the union of Śiva and Śakti in consciousness, for qualified initiates; one born of such a union is 'yoginībhū', a vessel of knowledge (29.162-163). Summary only.

name: The twelve Kālīs of the Krama

definitions.definition: Twelve goddesses as the phases of cognition: Sṛṣṭikālī, Raktakālī, Sthitināśakālī, Yamakālī, Saṃhārakālī, Mṛtyukālī, Rudrakālī, Mārtaṇḍakālī, Paramārkakālī, Kālāgnirudrakālī, Mahākālakālī, Mahābhairavacaṇḍograghorakālī (TĀ 4.148-172; Kramastotra 15-27).

notes: The first six names and the phases are confirmed by TĀ 4.148-154 and the Kramastotra; the forms of names 7-12 (esp. Rudrakālī vs Bhadrakālī, and the full name of the twelfth) are reconstructed - moderate confidence.

definitions.definition: Every cognition unfolds as emission (sṛṣṭi), persistence (sthiti), withdrawal (saṃhāra) and the nameless (anākhya), in the object, the means of knowledge and the subject - twelve Kālīs in all (TĀ 4.145, 4.148-172).

name: The five flows (pañcavāha) of goddesses

definitions.definition: Vyomavāmeśvarī, Khecarī, Dikcarī, Gocarī and Bhūcarī - the goddess-groups of consciousness, subject, inner organ, outer senses and objects - which delude the ignorant and liberate the knower (Kṣemarāja on PH 12, citing the Krama).

notes: The correlation of each group with a level is recalled from Kṣemarāja's commentary; low confidence.

definitions.definition: Known through the Trika: Mata scriptures reject the samaya rules and lineage-based exclusions in favour of realizing one's own unbounded awareness, and rank between Dakṣiṇa and Kula (or between Kula and Trika) in the hierarchy of revelations.
